title: Workers and the Workplace
gist: This is a RAND topic-hub/index page aggregating recent research on labor markets rather than a single article; the most investable thread running through the linked items is that AI-driven labor displacement threatens the federal tax base and is prompting proposals for tax-code reform.

themes.theme: AI and the federal tax base

insights.claim: RAND researchers argue that AI-driven automation could sharply reduce U.S. federal revenue by displacing labor, especially in scenarios where displaced workers are not reemployed or where AI deployment is cheap relative to human labor.
insights.speaker: RAND Corporation
insights.so_what: A structural erosion of labor-tax revenue from AI substitution is a macro tail risk for U.S. fiscal policy and could accelerate debate on new tax bases (e.g., taxing capital/AI output instead of wages).
insights.quote: Artificial intelligence (AI) replacing human labor could sharply reduce U.S. federal revenue, especially if workers are not reemployed or AI is cheap.
insights.locator: Federal Revenue When AI Replaces Labor summary

insights.claim: RAND researchers propose a six-category framework of tax-code reform options intended to stabilize federal revenue and protect jobs in the face of AI-driven labor substitution.
insights.speaker: RAND Corporation
insights.so_what: Watch for policy proposals shifting tax incidence away from labor and toward AI/capital/consumption as an early signal of how governments plan to fund fiscal gaps from automation.
insights.quote: The authors of this paper propose a six-category framework of tax code reform options that could stabilize revenue and protect jobs.
insights.locator: Tax Policy Options to Promote Employment and Stabilize Revenue in the AI Age

insights.claim: RAND named Jeffrey Wenger to a new two-year Distinguished Chair role focused specifically on AI's effects on workers, labor markets, public finances, and the broader economy, signaling institutional prioritization of this research area.
insights.speaker: RAND Corporation
insights.so_what: Indicates think-tank research bandwidth is being reallocated toward AI-labor-fiscal questions, a leading indicator that this topic will generate more policy proposals over the next two years.
insights.quote: In this new, two-year role, Wenger will advance RAND Education, Employment, and Infrastructure's research agenda on artificial intelligence, including its effects on workers, labor markets, public finances, and the broader economy.
insights.locator: Jeffrey Wenger Named RAND's Distinguished Chair, AI, Workers, and the Economy

insights.claim: RAND research suggests employers struggling to fill roles may be overlooking qualified candidates already close at hand rather than facing an absolute talent shortage.
insights.speaker: RAND Corporation
insights.so_what: Suggests labor-shortage narratives used to justify wage inflation or automation investment may be partly a hiring-practice/screening problem rather than a true supply shortfall.
insights.quote: Having Trouble Finding Good Workers? They're Right Under Your Nose

insights.claim: RAND is developing an occupation-based framework and interactive dashboard to estimate personal protective equipment (PPE) demand and workforce risk during future pandemics, intended to support national, state, and regional scenario planning.
insights.speaker: RAND Corporation
insights.so_what: Relevant to PPE manufacturers and health-policy investors tracking pandemic-preparedness procurement and stockpiling policy.
insights.quote: This report presents an occupation-based framework to estimate vital workforce size and personal protective equipment demand during a pandemic.
insights.locator: Personal Protective Equipment Prioritization and Demand
